info.title: Tallyhound mail layer contract
info.description:
What Tallyhound calls on the mail layer, and what it expects the layer to send back. Written by Tallyhound on November 25, 2026, before Neeter's own interface was known. Every path, field and status here is a proposal to agree with Neeter, not a description of Neeter's API. When the real interface is known, change apps/server/src/integrations/neeter/index.ts and this file together; apps/server/test/neeter.test.ts fails if they disagree.

White label: nothing the layer sends to a client may name the layer. Letters go from the CPA's own address, exactly as written, with no signature, footer, tracking pixel or 'sent by' line added. Only names reach the layer: a client's name and email address, a form's name and who issues it. Never a document, an amount or an identifier.

partnerKey.description: Tallyhound's own key (NEETER_PARTNER_KEY). Used only to make and revoke each firm's key and to ask who we are.

firmKey.description: One key per firm, limited to that firm's assistants. Tallyhound keeps it sealed with the firm's own encryption key and replaces it every 90 days (TH-NTR-9).

TaskStatus.description: Open: owed by the client. Completed: the client says it is sent and Tallyhound is checking. Done: verified by Tallyhound (set only by Tallyhound). On hold: no follow-ups. Canceled: not needed.

id.description: Unique per event. Tallyhound acts on each id once, however often it is delivered.

from.description: reply: the sender's address. Only replies on threads Tallyhound started, from senders on the firm's client list, should be sent; Tallyhound drops anything else.

to.description: bounce: the address that did not accept the letter.

text.description: reply: the plain text of the reply. Quoted earlier messages may be left in; Tallyhound strips them.

proposed_status.description: reply: the layer's own reading, if it has one. Advice only: Tallyhound's rules decide.

attachment_count.description: How many files the reply carried, whether or not they are included below.

content_base64.description: The file itself. Up to 25 MB each. Leave the list empty if files cannot be handed over: Tallyhound then asks a person to forward the email.

name.description: "Garcia, Maria 2026". Never a number that could identify the client.

closed.description: true once every document is in or the file is closed: no more follow-ups.

due_date.description: The morning Tallyhound plans the next letter. Advice for the layer's board; Tallyhound sends the letter itself unless NEETER_SEND=due_date.

title.description: The form and who issues it: "W-2 from Acme Logistics". No amounts, no identifiers.

note.description: Why, in words: "Held until March 15", "Passed the sniff test".

get.summary: Who the layer thinks we are. Used by the connection check.

post.description: Sign every call: header x-layer-signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>." followed by the exact body, keyed with NEETER_WEBHOOK_SECRET>. Calls older than five minutes are refused. 200 or 202 means received; anything else, retry with backoff for at least 24 hours. Send {"id":"...","type":"ping"} to test.
